_comment: Made-up findings for the documentation screenshots (make screenshots). Seeded through the HTTP API into a throwaway database by seed-demo.py. Nothing here is real operator data; keep it that way, because the images are published to the public wiki.

findings.summary: Quote code and comments verbatim in a brief instead of paraphrasing them
findings.suggestion: Where a brief asserts what code or a comment says, quote it verbatim rather than paraphrasing, and say which failure paths were tested and which are left for the reviewer.
findings.rationale: A brief described a comment as recording a caveat it did not contain. The reviewer spent a round establishing that the paraphrase had no source.

findings.summary: State-sync briefs name every Notes cell and journal note as a literal string
findings.suggestion: Require every state-sync brief to give the PROGRESS.md Notes cell and the FLIGHT-RECORDER note as literal strings, so the sync agent transcribes rather than composes.
findings.rationale: One brief named the journal note but not the Notes cell, and the two records that should corroborate each other were worded differently.

findings.summary: Label every figure in a brief as measured or carried from a report
findings.suggestion: Label each figure a brief supplies with its provenance: measured now with the command shown, or carried from an earlier report and to be re-derived.
findings.rationale: A figure presented as measured had been copied from a developer's report and was wrong by two; the error reached the audit journal.

findings.summary: Mark a diagnosis in a brief as a hypothesis with the observable that confirms it
findings.suggestion: State a diagnosis as a hypothesis, name the observable that would confirm it, and list the suspected files as starting points rather than scope.
findings.rationale: A brief classified a defect as a repaint problem; the cause was elsewhere and the named files bounded the search.

findings.summary: Give absolute paths when more than one checkout is open
findings.suggestion: When a session exposes more than one working directory or checkout, give file paths in briefs as absolute paths.
findings.rationale: A reviewer searched blind for a relative path that resolved under neither of two open working directories.

findings.summary: Name absolute paths in briefs when two checkouts exist
findings.suggestion: Name the absolute path to a repository in any brief that cites a file by relative path, when two checkouts exist on the machine.
findings.rationale: Same failure as an earlier finding, on a different mission.

findings.summary: Pair every empty-result check with a control that can return non-zero
findings.suggestion: A check whose pass condition is an empty result is paired, in the same invocation, with a control proven to return a non-empty result under the same filter.
findings.rationale: A case-sensitive grep returned nothing and nearly produced a false discrepancy report; only a positive control caught it.

findings.summary: Show a checker failing on corrupted input before believing its PASS
findings.suggestion: Before a structural check's PASS is accepted, run it against a deliberately corrupted copy and show it fails.
findings.rationale: Three checks across two missions could not fail on the inputs they were given.

findings.summary: A verification brief names the command that could falsify the claim
findings.suggestion: Write verification briefs as the command whose output could falsify the property, not as the property to confirm.
findings.rationale: A sweep phrased as 'confirm there is one table' confirmed it; the command that counted tables would have found three.

findings.summary: Ask what the laziest conforming work looks like before sending a gate
findings.suggestion: After drafting an acceptance gate, describe the weakest work that would satisfy it; if that work still has the defect, rewrite the gate.
findings.rationale: One gate took four rounds because each wording admitted a test that reproduced the wiring inside itself.

findings.summary: Review briefs carry the reviewed step's own diff
findings.suggestion: Every review brief pastes the diff hunks of the step under review; a reviewer with no shell cannot produce them.
findings.rationale: The reviewer asked for diffs in five separate notes in one mission.

findings.summary: Fix-round reviews carry the previous review's findings in full
findings.suggestion: A brief for a re-review carries the previous review's findings forward in full and by number, including closed ones.
findings.rationale: A reviewer was handed five of its own seven findings with no sign that two were missing.

findings.summary: State which review claims are established and which must be re-derived
findings.suggestion: Label each claim in a review brief as already derived independently or resting only on the report under review.
findings.rationale: A brief passed one checked claim and one unchecked claim under the same heading.

findings.summary: Append journal rows with a shell redirect, never an editing tool
findings.suggestion: Append audit-journal rows with printf and >>, and forbid editing tools on the journal file outright.
findings.rationale: Every mid-file insertion came from an editing tool; every redirect append landed at the end.

findings.summary: Check the whole journal timestamp column is non-decreasing
findings.suggestion: Verify a new journal row by re-reading the whole timestamp column and asserting it never decreases.
findings.rationale: The one-row check could not see rows inserted above existing ones.

findings.summary: Ask whether each test would pass with the code under test deleted
findings.suggestion: For every new test, ask whether it would still pass if the code under test were deleted; if so, it measures the platform.
findings.rationale: Two tests passed for reasons unrelated to the code they named.

findings.summary: Plant a mutant per new invariant at the coding step
findings.suggestion: A step that writes a test for a new invariant also plants one mutant against it and shows the test failing.
findings.rationale: Mutation testing at review found a survivor the fixture could never have caught.

findings.summary: Fail, never skip, when the precondition a test exists for is absent
findings.suggestion: A test whose subject is missing fails rather than skipping itself.
findings.rationale: An end-to-end test skipped whenever the grant it was meant to exercise did not appear.

findings.summary: Sanitise every field that enters an approval card
findings.suggestion: Pass every field entering an approval card through the same sanitiser the transcript applies to tool output.
findings.rationale: The one surface that asks for consent was the one that rendered untrusted text unsanitised.

findings.summary: Show the grant scope the policy will actually record
findings.suggestion: Compute the scope shown on an approval card from the same value the policy stores.
findings.rationale: The card named a wider grant than the policy recorded.

runs.notes: Classified 20 findings into 7 categories. None left uncategorised; 0 marked LOW.

groups.title: Quote literal text in a brief; never paraphrase it
groups.summary: Where a brief depends on exact text — code, a comment, a state-record string — it quotes that text verbatim so the receiver transcribes rather than composes.

groups.title: Absolute paths when the path is ambiguous
groups.summary: A brief that names a file by relative path also gives the absolute path whenever more than one working directory or checkout exists.

recommendations.rationale: Not covered in bishop.md: the 'Writing briefs' section has no rule about quoting. The finding records a paraphrase with no source.
recommendations.proposed_change:
File: .claude/agents/bishop.md, section "Writing briefs"

ADD after the bullet on scope:
- Where a brief states what code, a comment or a record says, quote it verbatim
  in a fenced block. Never paraphrase text the receiver will act on.

recommendations.rationale: The state-sync checklist names the journal note but not the Notes cell; this closes the gap the finding describes.
Specific and implementable; no doctrine file mentions absolute paths.
Restates the earlier finding with less detail.
Not covered: no file requires provenance labels on figures. Three missions record the same failure.
Overlaps the review-practice rule on labelling claims; the operator should decide whether this belongs in bishop.md or the review skill.

proposals.title: Briefs quote text and records literally
proposals.applies_when: A change that writes a brief which depends on exact code, comment or state-record text.
proposals.rule: A brief MUST quote such text verbatim and MUST NOT paraphrase it or leave the receiver to recover it from a template.
proposals.rationale: A paraphrase with no source gets transcribed as fact.
proposals.reviewer_check: Does every quoted string in the brief match its source byte for byte?

runs.notes: 6 findings read, 2 groups. 4 approve, 1 supersede, 1 defer. 1 directive draft.

groups.title: A check is not trusted until it has been shown to fail
groups.summary: A structural check must be shown to fail on a deliberately bad input, and an empty-result check must be paired with a control that can return non-zero, before its PASS is believed.

recommendations.rationale: Both findings state one rule; the skill's verification section has no positive-control requirement.
Same rule as c1, from the other direction.
Not covered in the code-review skill; the finding gives a concrete before and after.
Implementable as one paragraph in the closing checklist.

proposals.title: A check must fail on bad input before its PASS counts
proposals.applies_when: A change that adds or relies on a verification check, gate or acceptance criterion.
proposals.rule: A check MUST be shown to fail on a deliberately corrupted input before its PASS is accepted. A check whose pass condition is an empty result MUST be paired with a control proven to return a non-empty result under the same invocation.
proposals.rationale: Checks that cannot fail read as passes and hide real defects.
proposals.reviewer_check: Was every new check shown to fail on a bad input, and does every empty-result check have a positive control?
proposals.example: grep -c TODO src/ paired with grep -c func src/ returning non-zero.

runs.notes: 4 findings read, 1 group. 4 approve. 1 directive draft.

groups.title: Review briefs carry what the reviewer cannot produce
groups.summary: A reviewer with no shell needs the diff, the prior findings in full, and the provenance of every claim in the brief itself.

recommendations.rationale: Five requests in one mission; nothing in the skill requires the diff.
Closes the gap that hid two findings from their own reviewer.
Per-claim labels, not a general exhortation; implementable as written.

proposals.title: Review briefs carry the diff and prior findings
proposals.applies_when: A change that writes a brief for a code or document review.
proposals.rule: A review brief MUST paste the reviewed step's own diff and, for a re-review, the previous review's findings in full. Each claim it carries MUST be labelled as independently derived or resting on the report under review.
proposals.rationale: A reviewer without a shell cannot check what the brief does not contain.
proposals.reviewer_check: Does the brief contain the diff, the prior findings by number, and a provenance label on each claim?

runs.notes: 3 findings read, 1 group. 3 approve. 1 directive draft.
